The James Webb Space Telescope, also called JWST, works in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 region rather than in low Earth orbit. Its science instruments are NIRCam, NIRSpec, MIRI, and NIRISS. NIRCam takes near-infrared images, NIRSpec spreads that light into spectra, MIRI covers longer mid-infrared wavelengths, and NIRISS supports imaging and spectroscopy. A sunshield keeps the telescope cold enough for infrared work.
